rationale: An anonymous enum used as a MEMBER's type is a member path, exactly as an anonymous inline struct or union is. `typedef union { enum { A_ONE, A_TWO } first; int n; } U;` published `contains U -> A_ONE`, i.e. a member of `first` published as a member of the CONTAINER, so a consumer reading `U` sees `A_ONE` beside `first` and `n` and cannot learn that `first` is a type of its own with two enumerators. The two adjacent shapes were already correct, which is what makes this a defect rather than a design choice: a TAGGED inline enum keeps its own tag as the owner (`enum E { B_ONE } first;` -> `contains E -> B_ONE`), and an inline STRUCT composes the path via `inlineAggregateOwnerName` (#950/#951, pinned by `S.val.verbatim_str.str` in redis/src/call_reply.c). Measured over the four declared corpora (3,997 files): 17 members across 6 files -- curl's `pl_unix_substate` carries SEVEN inline enums in one union, so a single wrong owner there accounts for 35 `contains` edges; also `pl_winNT_substate` (3), `ftp_parselist_data` (1) in ftplistparser.c, `stub_gss_ctx_id_t_desc` in curl_gssapi.c, `OperationConfig` in tool_cfgable.h, and libgit2's `reftable_ref_record`, `reftable_log_record` and `refdb_reftable_stack_iterator`. This is #958's defect class reached from a different direction: the owner here is a REAL name, just the wrong one, so nothing looks broken and nothing crashes. The fix is one call to `inlineAggregateOwnerName` in `extractEnum`, placed BEFORE #961's scope rule so the scope rule still owns the function-local case.
